text: After this you can separate the user task from the support needed to enable it.

For education only; this is not legal, purchasing, financial or safety advice. Stage B turns a user task into a support workload. Ask what assets must do, how many are needed, and where and when they must be available. Describe duration, configurations, ordinary demand and exceptional peaks. The support team may not operate the equipment, but it must enable users to do so. Link each proposed support requirement to the user outcome it protects.

items: Ask users about real operations and training demand. You should see: Quantity, locations, timing and duration are captured. If not: Compare the response with actual use and ask about differences.
Specify each usage demand so it can be assessed. You should see: The needed output and conditions are clear. If not: Record a reasonable uncertainty range and its basis.

Connect support activities to the operating demands they enable. You should see: Each relevant target has an operating purpose. If not: Explain any need that does not translate into a support obligation.
Inferred: Forecast annual demand using likely operating activity, noting the difference between routine use, planned increases and short-notice peaks.

text: Find out demand, location and timing before planning support capacity.
Uncertain workload requires an explicit range, confidence estimate or surge assumption.
